title: alibaba/skill-up — An evaluation and evolution tool for Agent Skills.
content:
Evaluate Agent Skills, agents, and workspaces. Evolve Skills with evidence.
English | 中文
📖 User Manual · 用户手册
skill-up is a CLI for evaluating Agent Skills, agents, and their workspaces. It runs declarative cases against an Agent Engine, grades the response and workspace changes, and produces reports locally or in CI.
- Skill evaluation measures a Skill's behavior across cases and can compare runs with and without the Skill.
- Agent evaluation runs the same cases without installing a Skill, so you can assess an engine or custom agent on its own.
- Workspace evaluation checks how an agent works with files and repositories, using case fixtures or an existing local workspace.
- Skill evolution uses skill-upper to inspect failures, repair or expand the eval suite, and rerun skill-up through conversation.
- Eval-to-Evolution Loop with skill-upper: Create evals through natural conversation, diagnose failures, automatically repair or expand cases, and rerun skill-up until the eval suite evolves.
- Declarative Eval Config: Define evaluation environment, engine, model, and cases through YAML (eval.yaml +cases/*.yaml ).
- Environment Provisioning: Prepare a local, Docker, or OpenSandbox runtime for each case, install configured real or mocked MCP servers into supported Agent Engines, and upload context.repo_fixture andcontext.files into the workspace.
- Skill-Optional Runs and Workspace Cases: Evaluate an agent without a Skill, prepare repository fixtures per case, or run against an existing local workspace with --workspace .
- Multi-Engine Support: Works with Qoder CLI, Claude Code, and Codex as built-in Agent Engines, plus user-defined agents via engine.custom (local transport — see docs/design/custom-engine.md).
- DeepSeek Harness Plugin: Use the bundled skill-upper Skill, opt-in durable observation capture, approval-gated regression cases, isolated runs, and status comparison to verify evidence-backed Skill improvements. Seeplugins/dsh-skill-up .
- Flexible Judging: Supports rule_based ,script , andagent_judge evaluation strategies.
- Structured Reports: Outputs Anthropic-compatible grading.json ,benchmark.json ,benchmark.md , plusresult.json , JUnit XML, and HTML reports.
- Anthropic Compatible: Import evals.json viaskill-up import , or auto-detect with--auto .
- CI-Ready: Designed for local development and continuous integration pipelines.
Harness engineering treats an agent's environment, tools, constraints, and feedback loops as parts of the system to design and improve. Behavioral evals make expected agent actions observable and help catch regressions. skill-up contributes evaluation and feedback to this work: repeatable prompts and workspace setups, checks on responses, tool calls, and file changes, and structured reports.
For Skills, the official Agent Skills evaluation guide describes a further loop: run with and without the Skill, grade outputs, aggregate results, and iterate. skill-up supports these workflows:
- Replaces ad hoc run folders with a declarative eval.yaml +cases/*.yaml format.
- Closes the improvement loop: skill-upper can interpret failed reports, repair or add eval cases, and drive the next skill-up run through conversation.
- Automates workspace setup, optional Skill installation, Agent Engine invocation, judging, and report generation.
- Supports multiple engines (claude_code ,codex ,qodercli ,qwen_code ) instead of tying the workflow to one client.
- Keeps compatibility with Anthropic-style evals.json while adding richer judges, CI-friendly commands, and structured reports.
For Skill evolution, use skill-upper, the Agent Skill shipped in this repository. It lets your AI agent create evals, run skill-up, understand failures, fix the Skill or its evals, add regression coverage, and repeat the loop through conversation.
For repository development, skills/skill-upper/ is the only editable source.
Plugin bundles are generated into ignored build directories rather than tracked
copies or symlinks; run make bundle-plugins when preparing them locally.
make package-plugins VERSION=<version> creates self-contained Codex and DSH
archives. Tagged GitHub releases attach both archives and their checksums; this
repository does not publish either plugin to an external marketplace or npm.
# Codex, global install
npx skills add https://github.com/alibaba/skill-up/tree/main/skills/skill-upper -g -a codex -y
# Claude Code, global install
npx skills add https://github.com/alibaba/skill-up/tree/main/skills/skill-upper -g -a claude-code -y
You normally do not need to install skill-up first. skill-upper checks for the CLI when it runs and guides the agent through installation if needed.
Open a project that contains your Skill's SKILL.md in Codex, Claude Code, or
another compatible Agent, then ask:
Use skill-upper to evaluate this Skill.
Read SKILL.md, identify its most important behaviors, create realistic eval
cases with appropriate judges, validate the configuration, and run skill-up.
Summarize the results and the highest-impact failures.
skill-upper creates the declarative eval suite and drives the CLI for you:
my-skill/
  SKILL.md
  evals/
    eval.yaml
    cases/
      <case-id>.yaml
my-skill-workspace/
  iteration-1/
    result.json
Continue in the same conversation:
Review the latest skill-up results. For each failure, determine whether the
Skill or the eval is wrong. Fix SKILL.md and supporting files, or repair the
eval case and judge as appropriate. Add regression cases for the bugs you
found, rerun skill-up, and continue until the important behaviors pass.
This is the evolution loop: reports become fixes, fixes become regression cases, and every iteration makes the Skill and its eval suite stronger.
You can still install the CLI directly and hand-write eval.yaml and case
files:
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alibaba/skill-up/main/install.sh | bash
See the official documentation for Getting Started, Writing Evals, CLI Reference, and User Configuration. Windows-specific setup and limitations are covered in the Windows guide.
An agent-only eval does not need SKILL.md. Set skills: [] explicitly: when
skills is omitted and skill-up finds a SKILL.md above the config, it installs
that Skill automatically. Put eval.yaml and case files under evals/, then
pass the config path explicitly. Case and fixture paths resolve from the
discovered Skill root, or from the directory containing evals/ if none is found.
# evals/eval.yaml
schema_version: v1alpha1
environment:
  type: none
skills: []
engine:
  name: codex
cases:
  files:
    - evals/cases/agent-response.yaml# evals/cases/agent-response.yaml
input:
  prompt: Reply with READY.
expect:
  must_contain: [READY]skill-up validate ./evals/eval.yaml
skill-up run ./evals/eval.yaml
For repository tasks, a case can use context.repo_fixture to prepare a fresh
workspace and expect or a judge to check the result. To evaluate an agent in
an already prepared local directory, use a case written for that directory and
run skill-up run ./evals/eval.yaml --workspace /path/to/project --parallelism 1.
The existing directory is preserved, but the agent and case setup can change
its contents. This option requires environment.type: none, one case at a time,
and benchmark mode off. See Writing Evals
and the CLI Reference.
skill-up auto-loads an optional user-level config that supplies default OpenTelemetry env vars and per-environment runtime kwargs. The embedded defaults are empty; downstream consumers maintain their own config file.
embed (empty) < user (~/.config/skill-up/config.yaml) < project ($PWD/.skill-up.yaml) < explicit (--config)
Missing files at the user and project layers are silently skipped; a missing --config path is a hard error. A corrupt config at any layer also fails the run.
skill-up init                            # writes a template to ~/.config/skill-up/config.yaml (XDG-aware)
skill-up init --local                    # writes a template to $PWD/.skill-up.yaml
skill-up init --print

report.summary: Alibaba open-sources skill-up, a CLI that evaluates and evolves Agent Skills via declarative evals, multi-engine runs, and an AI-driven repair loop.
report.background: Agent Skills — reusable instruction folders like SKILL.md — have spread quickly across Claude Code, Codex, Qoder CLI and similar engines, but quality control has lagged. Teams typically test Skills by hand, dropping ad-hoc run folders and eyeballing outputs, which makes regressions easy to miss. Anthropic's own Agent Skills evaluation guide recommends running a Skill with and without it installed, grading outputs and iterating, yet few toolchains automate that loop. Alibaba's skill-up arrives in this gap, borrowing ideas from 'harness engineering', which treats an agent's environment, tools, constraints and feedback loops as designable parts of the system. By making expected agent behaviour observable through repeatable prompts, workspace fixtures and structured reports, skill-up aims to turn Skill development from intuition into an evidence-backed engineering practice that also fits CI pipelines.
key_points: Declarative, CI-ready evaluation: skill-up replaces ad-hoc run folders with a YAML format (eval.yaml plus cases/*.yaml) describing environment, engine, model and test cases. It provisions local, Docker or OpenSandbox runtimes, installs real or mocked MCP servers, and grades responses, tool calls and workspace file changes, emitting grading.json, benchmark.json, JUnit XML and HTML reports.

Three evaluation scopes: Skill evaluation measures a Skill's behaviour and compares runs with and without it installed; agent evaluation assesses an engine or custom agent on its own; workspace evaluation checks how an agent handles files and repositories using fixtures or an existing local directory via --workspace. Judges can be rule-based, script-based or LLM-based.

The evolution loop via skill-upper: a bundled Agent Skill that lets a coding agent write evals, run skill-up, read failure reports, decide whether the Skill or the eval case is wrong, fix one, add regression cases and rerun — repeating conversationally until important behaviours pass. This turns reports into fixes and fixes into permanent regression coverage.

Multi-engine and Anthropic compatibility: built-in support covers Claude Code, Codex, Qoder CLI and Qwen Code, with custom engines via engine.custom. It imports existing evals.json files or auto-detects them, so teams already using Anthropic-style evaluation formats can adopt skill-up without rewriting their test suites.

Distribution and packaging: skill-upper installs with a single npx skills add command for Codex or Claude Code and checks for the CLI itself. Repositories generate self-contained plugin archives via make commands, and tagged GitHub releases attach the archives and checksums rather than publishing to an external marketplace.
report.impact: For the AI industry, skill-up pushes Agent Skills toward measurable engineering rather than prompt folklore, giving vendors and platform teams a neutral yardstick for comparing engines and Skill quality. For developers, it lowers the cost of maintaining Skill libraries: regressions get caught in CI, and the skill-upper loop means a coding agent can repair failing Skills and grow the test suite without a human writing every case. Multi-engine support also reduces lock-in, letting teams validate the same Skill across Claude Code, Codex and Qwen Code. For regular users, better-tested Skills should mean fewer silent failures and more predictable agent behaviour, though the benefits arrive indirectly and depend on Skill authors adopting the tooling.
report.tools: Start with alibaba/skill-up itself (CLI plus the bundled skill-upper Skill, installed via npx skills add). Compare with Anthropic's Agent Skills evaluation guidance and evals.json format. Related infrastructure worth watching: OpenSandbox and Docker for isolated runtimes, MCP servers for tool mocking, Codex and Claude Code as reference engines, and Qoder CLI or Qwen Code for multi-engine testing. For judging, pair rule-based checks with an LLM-as-judge and pipe JUnit XML into your existing CI. Also useful: OpenTelemetry config support for run observability.
